pool.text: Travelers known as the Denny Party arrived at Alki Point from Portland.
The growing settlement moved to Elliott Bay and received its final name.
The brief Puget Sound War culminated in the Battle of Seattle.
The city re-incorporated with a mayor-council government structure.
The Great Seattle Fire destroyed the central business district.
The Seattle Times, the lone daily newspaper in the city, was founded.
Bertha Knight Landes became the first female mayor of a major American city.
The 5th Avenue Theatre opened and began staging Broadway-style musical shows.
The Henry Art Gallery opened as the first public art museum in Washington.
The Seattle Art Museum opened its doors to the public.
The city celebrated restored prosperity by hosting the Century 21 Exposition World's Fair.
Seattle saw local developments of modern paramedic services with the establishment of Medic One.
The first location for Starbucks Coffee opened at Pike Place Market.
The Seattle Aquarium opened on the downtown waterfront.
The Wah Mee massacre resulted in thirteen killings in an illegal gambling club.
The Goodwill Games were held in the city.
Sherry Harris was elected as a Seattle city councilor in United States history.
Leaders from APEC gathered in Seattle for a major international summit.
Democrat Adam Smith began representing part of southeastern Seattle in the 9th congressional district.
The city government committed to becoming North America's first climate neutral city.
